description: A user procedure declared `Double` (mixed case) called as `DOUBLE` with too few arguments raises ol-not-enough-inputs whose params.callable is the definition's declared spelling `Double`, not the call site casing nor a lowercasing — case-insensitive identifiers can never make the call spelling the diagnostic identity (spec/error-model.md:255-260), and a mixed-case declaration is what distinguishes the declared-spelling rule from mere lowercasing (matching check-side issue #874). Issue #1005. Issue #815: `execute()` now runs Layer 1 and Layer 2 before Phase 2 and refuses a program carrying an `error`-severity finding (`spec/execution-model.md:659-664`), so no event is emitted and the diagnostic delivered here is the CHECK's. The runtime's own copy of the rule still exists and still runs — under the `runUnchecked` opt-out — and is collapsed into the check's by the de-duplication rule (`spec/execution-model.md:741-748`), which is why only one report survives and it reads `stage: "semantic"`.
